newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Aug trade surplus at record C$4.02 bln.
newsitem.headline: Canada Aug trade surplus at record C$4.02 bln.

text.p: Canada's merchandise trade surplus rose in August to a record $4.02 billion from C$2.89 billion in July, revised from C$3.07 billion, Statistics Canada said on Friday.
Note: Figures in billions of current Canadian dollars, on a balance of payments basis, seasonally adjusted.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a surplus of C$3.37 billion in August. The survey also forecast imports of C$19.6 billion and exports of C$22.9 billion in August.
Statistics Canada said exports rose by 2.7 percent in August, mainly due to strong vehicle shipments and a rebound in the sales of grain and other agricultural products.
Stronger automotive exports accounted for a record C$19.17 billion exports to the United States in August. Shipments to all other trading partners, except Japan, also rose, Statistics Canada said.
Statistics Canada also said imports weakened in August, mostly due to slower shipments of machinery, industrial goods and auto parts.
Canada's trade surplus has risen steadily as a proportion of gross domestic product, reaching 4.5 percent in the second quarter of 1996 compared to 0.5 percent in 1991, the agency said.

The upward trend in exports since the second quarter of 1995 largely reflects economic strength in the United States, Canada's largest trading partner. About C$1 billion worth of goods crosses the border between the two countries every day.
By contrast, Canada's imports have remained flat in the past year, reflecting relatively weaker domestic demand, Statistics Canada said.
